## Objectives

In this class we explore and describe three related datasets. the data includes a cohort of individuals, their Ischaemic Heart Disease (IHD) diagnoses and link to the death registry. The data is derived from (https://github.com/theresenoest/HEL3054-MedicalData).

During this session we will:

- Download the datasets
- Explore each dataset and find out what it contains
- Understand how the datasets relate to each other

We start by importing relevant libraries

```{r initial settings}
# Import libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(tableone)
library(here)
```

## 1. The datasets

The three datasets are in the following GitHub repository: github.com/jd-otero/HEL3054_MedDataInitialExploration:

- [cohort_baseline.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jd-otero/HEL3054_MedDataInitialExploration/main/data/raw/cohort_baseline.csv)
- [registry_diagnoses.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jd-otero/HEL3054_MedDataInitialExploration/main/data/raw/registry_diagnoses.csv)
- [death_followup.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jd-otero/HEL3054_MedDataInitialExploration/main/data/raw/death_followup.csv)

We will read them straight from GitHub using the following code:

```{r download data}
repo <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jd-otero/HEL3054_MedDataInitialExploration/main/data/raw"

raw_url_cohort <- paste(repo,"cohort_baseline.csv", sep = "/")
raw_url_diagnosis <- paste(repo, "registry_diagnoses.csv", sep = "/")
raw_url_death <- paste(repo, "death_followup.csv", sep = "/")

# Read directly from the URLs.
cohort <- read.csv(raw_url_cohort)
diagnosis <- read.csv(raw_url_diagnosis)
death <- read.csv(raw_url_death)

write_csv(cohort, here("data", "raw", "cohort_baseline.csv"))
write_csv(diagnosis, here("data", "raw", "registry_diagnoses.csv"))
write_csv(death, here("data", "raw", "death_followup.csv"))
```

### 1.1 A first look

- What does each dataset seem to contain?
- How many rows does each dataset have?
- What does one row represent in each dataset? Does a row mean the same thing in all three?

*Hint: `head()`, `nrow()` and `n_distinct()`.*

```{r first-look}
head(cohort)
head(diagnosis)
head(death)

nrow(cohort)
nrow(diagnosis)
nrow(death)

n_distinct(cohort$person_id)
n_distinct(diagnosis$person_id)
n_distinct(death$person_id)
```

## 2. Initial exploration

### 2.1 Types, missing values and structure

Identify the data types, the missing data and the structure of each dataset.

*Hint: `str()` and `is.na()`.*

```{r initial-exploration}
# General structure
str(cohort)
str(diagnosis)
str(death)

# Missing values per column
colSums(is.na(cohort))
colSums(is.na(diagnosis))
colSums(is.na(death))
```
